rules.principle: Begin from one explicit state record that owns priority, completion and prior evidence.
Inspect the latest default-branch CI before taking planned work; a real red result takes priority.
Finish one bounded item with implementation, tests and documentation instead of leaving several partial edits.
Break the guarded behavior in a disposable copy and require the expected assertion to fail.
Run the repository's exact gate commands and scopes; a similar local command is not equivalent.
Keep parallel or adversarial work off the commit tree, review every diff hunk and verify the clone-visible tree.
Fetch before pushing, prove the remote default branch is an ancestor and never force-push through divergence.
Write to production only inside the authorized scope, with backup, atomic replacement and origin plus public verification.
Trace quantitative claims to evidence, carry their conditions and never edit the record to rescue the story.
Do not read, print, commit or move credentials unless the user explicitly authorizes that exact secret operation.
Prepare release, issue and announcement drafts, but leave every public submission or publication action to the user.
Record the commit, verification and external status in the state record before starting the next item.
